  1200	    #[test]
  1201	    fn scoped_undo_group_nested_returns_err() {
  1202	        // Nested start_undo_group_scoped (without ending the
  1203	        // outer first) must return Err, just like the non-
  1204	        // scoped variant.
  1205	        let mut s = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
  1206	        let _guard1 = s.start_undo_group_scoped().unwrap();
  1207	        // Cannot call start_undo_group_scoped on s while guard1
  1208	        // is alive (borrow checker). Test the equivalent via
  1209	        // the underlying method on the guarded session:
  1210	        // ... actually the borrow checker prevents this at
  1211	        // compile time, which is GOOD — the RAII guard makes
  1212	        // accidental nesting a compile error rather than a
  1213	        // runtime error. Document this fact:
  1214	        // let _guard2 = s.start_undo_group_scoped(); // <-- borrow error
  1215	        //
  1216	        // To verify the runtime contract still holds for
  1217	        // non-scoped nesting, drop guard1 then re-test:
  1218	        drop(_guard1);
  1219	        // Now manually open a non-scoped group + try to start
  1220	        // a scoped one.
  1221	        s.start_undo_group().unwrap();
  1222	        let is_err = {
  1223	            let result = s.start_undo_group_scoped();
  1224	            let is_err = matches!(&result, Err(CollabSessionError::Undo(_)));
  1225	            // Drop `result` here so its potential Ok-arm borrow
  1226	            // doesn't extend into the `s.end_undo_group()` call.
  1227	            drop(result);
  1228	            is_err
  1229	        };
  1230	        assert!(is_err, "scoped variant must also return Err on nested call");
  1231	        s.end_undo_group();
  1232	    }

  1311	    #[test]
  1312	    fn undo_retracts_visible_op_from_op_log_len() {
  1313	        // Codex 5.4 V1 audit HIGH closure: after undo, the visible
  1314	        // `"ops"` LoroList shrinks (Loro retracts the original op).
  1315	        // Pre-closure `OpLog::cached_len` was stale; post-closure
  1316	        // `len()` queries Loro directly so it tracks correctly.
  1317	        let mut s = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
  1318	        s.append_op(put_value(0, 0, 0, 1.0)).unwrap();
  1319	        s.append_op(put_value(0, 0, 1, 2.0)).unwrap();

  1321	        assert_eq!(s.op_log().iter().count(), 2);
  1322	
  1323	        assert!(s.undo().unwrap());
  1324	        // op_count + iter().count() must agree post-undo.
  1325	        assert_eq!(s.op_log().iter().count(), s.op_count());
  1326	        assert_eq!(s.op_count(), 1, "visible op count must shrink to 1");
  1327	
  1328	        // Redo restores.
  1329	        assert!(s.redo().unwrap());
  1330	        assert_eq!(s.op_log().iter().count(), s.op_count());
  1331	        assert_eq!(s.op_count(), 2);
  1332	    }

  1337	        // undoable by the reborn peer (Loro local-only undo
  1338	        // semantics — `loro-internal::undo:615-643` composes
  1339	        // imported events into `remote_event` rather than pushing

  1350	            0,

  1352	        );

  1358	    #[test]
  1359	    fn local_undo_after_remote_merge_preserves_remote_ops() {
  1360	        // Codex 5.4 V1 audit C2 closure: peer A appends, B merges A's
  1361	        // bytes, A undoes A's append, B re-merges. After re-merge, B
  1362	        // sees A's op as retracted (Loro propagates the undo's inverse
  1363	        // through the CRDT). The remote contribution from B's own
  1364	        // appends survives unchanged.
  1365	        let base = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
  1366	        let base_bytes = base.export_bytes().unwrap();
  1367	
  1368	        let mut peer_a = CollabSession::from_snapshot(PeerId::new(0xa1), &base_bytes).unwrap();
  1369	        peer_a.append_op(put_value(0, 0, 0, 10.0)).unwrap();
  1370	
  1371	        let mut peer_b = CollabSession::from_snapshot(PeerId::new(0xb1), &base_bytes).unwrap();
  1372	        peer_b.append_op(put_value(0, 1, 0, 20.0)).unwrap();
  1373	        peer_b.merge_bytes(&peer_a.export_bytes().unwrap()).unwrap();
  1374	        let b_count_before = peer_b.op_count();
  1375	        assert!(b_count_before >= 2, "B sees A's + B's ops");
  1376	
  1377	        // A undoes its append. iter().count() shrinks on A.
  1378	        assert!(peer_a.undo().unwrap());
  1379	        let a_iter = peer_a.op_log().iter().count();
  1380	        assert!(
  1381	            a_iter < 1 || a_iter == 0,
  1382	            "A's visible ops shrink post-undo, got {a_iter}"
  1383	        );
  1384	
  1385	        // B merges A's post-undo state. A's retract should propagate.
  1386	        peer_b.merge_bytes(&peer_a.export_bytes().unwrap()).unwrap();
  1387	        let b_iter_after = peer_b.op_log().iter().count();
  1388	        assert!(
  1389	            b_iter_after < b_count_before,
  1390	            "B's visible op count must shrink after merging A's undo (was {b_count_before}, now {b_iter_after})"
  1391	        );
  1392	        // But B still sees its OWN op — undo is local-only.
  1393	        assert!(
  1394	            b_iter_after >= 1,
  1395	            "B's own op must survive A's local undo (local-only semantics)"
  1396	        );
  1397	    }

  1544	    #[test]
  1545	    fn poll_remote_treats_closed_as_graceful_end_of_stream() {
  1546	        // Codex+Opus 5.5 V2 V1 audit closure: pin partial-merge-
  1547	        // then-Closed semantics. The trait contract guarantees
  1548	        // Closed only after queue drains; CollabSession::poll_remote
  1549	        // returns Ok(merged) on Closed (NOT Err) so the caller sees
  1550	        // the merge count.
  1551	        use crate::transport::LoopbackTransport;
  1552	        let (tx_a, mut tx_b) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
  1553	        let mut s = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
  1554	
  1555	        // Queue 3 snapshots in tx_a's inbox.
  1556	        let snapshot = {
  1557	            let other = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(2)).unwrap();
  1558	            other.export_bytes().unwrap()
  1559	        };
  1560	        for _ in 0..3 {
  1561	            tx_b.send(&snapshot).unwrap();
  1562	        }
  1563	        // Close tx_a's endpoint. Per trait contract, A.try_recv
  1564	        // drains 3 queued blobs first, then returns Closed.
  1565	        tx_a.close();
  1566	        s.attach_transport(tx_a);
  1567	
  1568	        let drained = s.poll_remote().unwrap();
  1569	        assert_eq!(
  1570	            drained, 3,
  1571	            "poll_remote must drain all queued blobs even when transport is closed"
  1572	        );
  1573	        // Next poll: queue is empty + closed → still Ok(0) (graceful).
  1574	        let drained2 = s.poll_remote().unwrap();
  1575	        assert_eq!(drained2, 0);
  1576	    }

  1655	    #[test]
  1656	    fn two_sessions_exchange_state_via_loopback_transport() {
  1657	        // Phase 5.5 V1 integration: drive two CollabSessions
  1658	        // through a LoopbackTransport pair. V1 doesn't auto-
  1659	        // flush appends to the transport (5.5 V2 work), so the
  1660	        // test manually exports/sends/recvs/merges to verify the
  1661	        // wire actually carries the right bytes.
  1662	        use crate::transport::{LoopbackTransport, Transport};
  1663	        let (mut tx_a, mut tx_b) = LoopbackTransport::pair();
  1664	
  1665	        let base = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
  1666	        let base_bytes = base.export_bytes().unwrap();
  1667	
  1668	        let mut peer_a = CollabSession::from_snapshot(PeerId::new(0xa), &base_bytes).unwrap();
  1669	        let mut peer_b = CollabSession::from_snapshot(PeerId::new(0xb), &base_bytes).unwrap();
  1670	
  1671	        // Peer A appends an op, exports, sends over the wire.
  1672	        peer_a.append_op(put_value(0, 0, 0, 42.0)).unwrap();
  1673	        let a_bytes = peer_a.export_bytes().unwrap();
  1674	        tx_a.send(&a_bytes).unwrap();
  1675	
  1676	        // Peer B drains the transport and merges.
  1677	        let received = tx_b
  1678	            .try_recv()
  1679	            .unwrap()
  1680	            .expect("tx_b must receive A's bytes");
  1681	        assert_eq!(received, a_bytes);
  1682	        peer_b.merge_bytes(&received).unwrap();
  1683	        assert!(peer_b.op_count() >= 1, "B must see A's op after merge");
  1684	
  1685	        // Reverse direction: B appends, sends to A.
  1686	        peer_b.append_op(put_value(0, 1, 0, 99.0)).unwrap();
  1687	        tx_b.send(&peer_b.export_bytes().unwrap()).unwrap();
  1688	        let b_received = tx_a
  1689	            .try_recv()
  1690	            .unwrap()
  1691	            .expect("tx_a must receive B's bytes");
  1692	        peer_a.merge_bytes(&b_received).unwrap();
  1693	
  1694	        // After the exchange, both sessions converge on the same op count.
  1695	        assert_eq!(peer_a.op_count(), peer_b.op_count());
  1696	    }

  1713	    #[test]
  1714	    fn sweep_presence_clears_all_entries_and_returns_count() {
  1715	        // Phase 5.6 V2: sweep_presence removes ALL presence
  1716	        // entries (including own + remote peers) and returns the
  1717	        // count cleared. Closes the V1 "stale presence after
  1718	        // .qbook reload" known limitation as a caller-opt-in.
  1719	        let mut s = CollabSession::new(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap();
  1720	        s.update_presence(PresenceState::at_cell(0, 0, 0)).unwrap();
  1721	        // Simulate a remote peer's presence via the lower-level
  1722	        // OpLog write (we don't have a multi-peer setup in this
  1723	        // test).
  1724	        s.log
  1725	            .presence_set("0000000000000002", r#"{"sheet":1,"row":2,"col":3,"selection_end_row":2,"selection_end_col":3,"typing":false}"#)
  1726	            .unwrap();
  1727	        assert_eq!(s.peers_with_presence().unwrap().len(), 2);
  1728	
  1729	        let cleared = s.sweep_presence().unwrap();
  1730	        assert_eq!(cleared, 2, "sweep returns count of removed entries");
  1731	        assert!(s.peers_with_presence().unwrap().is_empty());
  1732	        assert_eq!(s.peer_presence(PeerId::new(1)).unwrap(), None);
  1733	        assert_eq!(s.peer_presence(PeerId::new(2)).unwrap(), None);
  1734	
  1735	        // Subsequent update_presence works (sweep didn't corrupt

    10	# Phase 5.3 — Conflict Resolution Semantics
    11	
    12	## Background
    13	
    14	Phase 5.1 audit-locked the conflict-matrix table at `crdt-data-model.md:311-334` and explicitly deferred two items to 5.3:
    15	
    16	1. **Conflict-matrix formalization** — 7 op-pair rows whose default behavior is "last-in-causal-order wins" (Loro's Fugue/origin-based merge, NOT Lamport LWW). Most are correct by Loro's design; 5.3 makes them load-bearing via test pins.
    17	2. **Causality-aware rename-repair pass** — the actual hard work. Concurrent edits authored against an old sheet name produce `BindError::UnknownSheet → #NAME?` after merge (V1 limitation, D-3 shipped the mapping). 5.3 makes those formulas RESOLVE by rewriting their text post-merge.
    18	
    19	## Critical finding from code survey (replay.rs:486-532)
    20	
    21	**Concurrent RenameSheet currently HARD-FAILS replay** with `ReplayError::SheetRenameNameMismatch`. Two peers each renaming the same sheet (A: S1→S2, B: S1→S3 concurrent) → after Loro's causal-order merge, the second rename's `old_name = "S1"` doesn't match current state (now `S2`) → replay errors → unrecoverable state. This is a real gap unflagged by the design doc preview. **5.3 step 2 fixes this.**
    22	
    23	## Audit-locked design decisions (will be documented in 5-3-exit-packet.md)
    24	
    25	### D-5.3-1 — Repair pass invocation
    26	**Decision: caller-driven, NOT hooked into merge_bytes.** Standalone function `repair_sheet_rename_chain(workbook, log) -> RepairReport`. Caller invokes after `merge_bytes` + `replay_into` + before `recompute_all`. Matches existing pattern (replay + recompute are caller-driven; no magic in merge_bytes).
    27	
    28	**Alternative considered**: hook into `CollabSession::merge_bytes_with_repair`. Rejected because it couples merge to repair (callers may want manual control for batch-merge scenarios).
    29	
    30	### D-5.3-2 — Repair algorithm
    31	**Decision: chain-based, NOT causality-aware.** Build `(old_canonical → new_name)` chain by sheet_id from `Op::RenameSheet` ops in the log; walk all formulas; rewrite text via the existing `rewrite_formula_text_for_sheet_rename` helper (sheets.rs:37-60).
    32	
    33	**Why chain-based over causality-aware**:
    34	- Helper returns `None` on no-change → idempotent. A formula already-referencing the new name won't be rewritten.
    35	- Doesn't require exposing Loro causality types (frontiers, OpIds) in our public API. The survey confirmed `OpLog` exposes no causality query surface; adding one is a significant architectural change.
    36	- Covers the user-visible case: formula authored against old name post-merge gets rewritten.
    37	- Edge cases: rename-then-drop produces #NAME? (sheet gone) — correct. Rename-back (S1→S2→S1) produces identity chain — helper no-ops via canonical comparison.
    38	
    39	### D-5.3-3 — Concurrent RenameSheet policy (step 2 fix)
    40	**Decision: last-in-causal-order wins; second rename targets the current sheet name.** Replay case 3 (current ≠ old ≠ new) currently errors. New behavior:
    41	- Sheet still exists at id → apply rename to whatever the sheet currently is (peer's `old_name` is "what they thought was current"; if reality has moved on, rename current to new).
    42	- Sheet was dropped → existing `InvalidSheet` error (genuine corruption case).
    43	
    44	**Rationale**: matches the "last-in-causal-order wins" rule already documented for SetName. Avoids hard-failing replay on a policy decision. The sheet name converges deterministically because Loro's causal order is deterministic across peers.
    45	
    46	### D-5.3-4 — Repair pass module location
    47	**Decision: `crates/ql-collab/src/repair.rs` (NEW)**, re-exported as `ql_collab::repair_sheet_rename_chain`. Lives in ql-collab because:
    48	- Repair is a CRDT-merge concern, not a workbook concern. ql-storage shouldn't depend on it.
    49	- ql-collab is the natural orchestration layer that callers already use for merge.
    50	- Keeps ql-exec out of merge semantics (ql-exec is the producer-side runtime).
    51	
    52	### D-5.3-5 — Repair report shape
    53	**Decision**:
    54	```rust
    55	pub struct RepairReport {
    56	    pub formulas_rewritten: usize,
    57	    pub sheets_with_renames: Vec<(SheetId, Vec<(String, String)>)>, // (sheet, chain of old→new pairs)
    58	    pub unresolved: Vec<UnresolvedRepair>, // e.g., formula references sheet that was renamed AND dropped
    59	}
    60	```
    61	Surfaces what was done (for caller logging) + what couldn't be repaired (analogous to `XlsxExportReport.dropped_features`'s explicit-loss pattern). Per the no-fallbacks rule.
    62	
    63	### D-5.3-6 — Scope of repair
    64	**In scope**: `Op::RenameSheet` chains.
    65	**Out of scope (V1 → defer to 5.3 step 4 or later)**: `Op::RenameTable`, `Op::RenameColumn`. Same problem shape, but step 4 will determine if replay already handles them (DropTable currently → bind fails → #NAME? per D-3) or needs the same fix.
    66	**Permanently out of scope**: drop-table repair. There's no "old → new" mapping for the repair to follow; #NAME? is the correct outcome.
    67	
    68	### D-5.3-7 — Schema impact
    69	**Decision: NONE.** 5.3 is purely additive — runtime correctness fix. No `WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION` or `OPLOG_SCHEMA_VERSION` bump. Old workbooks load identically; repair is a new caller-invoked function with no on-disk format implications.
    70

     1	//! Replay an `OpLog` against a `Workbook`.
     2	//!
     3	//! Phase 2A.3.a (2026-05-12): single entry point `replay_into(&OpLog, &mut
     4	//! Workbook, &FunctionRegistry) -> Result<usize, ReplayError>`. Returns the
     5	//! count of ops successfully applied; on failure, returns
     6	//! `ReplayError::At { index, kind }` carrying the position of the failing
     7	//! op and the underlying failure. The workbook is left in a partial state
     8	//! on failure (callers decide whether to discard, recover, or recompute).
     9	//!
    10	//! ## Replay semantics
    11	//!
    12	//! Each `Op` variant maps to one `Workbook` mutation:
    13	//!
    14	//! - `PutValue` → `Workbook::put_at` (after row/col bounds check).
    15	//! - `PutFormula` → `Workbook::put_formula` (text only; replay does NOT
    16	//!   re-evaluate — that's a separate step the caller drives via
    17	//!   `WorkbookRuntime::recompute_all`).
    18	//! - `ClearFormula` → `Workbook::clear_formula`.
    19	//! - `SetName` → `Workbook::set_name`. Reserved names (e.g. `AI`) surface
    20	//!   as `ReplayError::NameRejected`.
    21	//! - `AddSheet` → `Workbook::add_sheet_with_chunk_rows`.
    22	//! - `BatchCommit` → recurse on each inner op. Index reporting flattens:
    23	//!   a failure inside a BatchCommit reports the inner op's overall
    24	//!   position (current outer index + offset).
    25	//!
    26	//! ## Idempotence
    27	//!
    28	//! `replay_into` is idempotent only in the trivial sense: replaying twice
    29	//! against the same starting workbook produces the same final state IFF
    30	//! the underlying mutation methods are themselves idempotent (and they
    31	//! are — `put_at` / `put_formula` / `clear_formula` / `set_name` /
    32	//! `add_sheet` all are). Callers wanting at-most-once semantics across
    33	//! sessions track replay state themselves (Phase 5+ work).
    34	//!
    35	//! ## `registry` parameter
    36	//!
    37	//! Passed for API symmetry with `WorkbookRuntime::new(&mut wb, &registry)`.
    38	//! 2A.3.a's replay doesn't use it (formula evaluation is deferred to a
    39	//! separate `recompute_all` call), but keeping the parameter stable here
    40	//! avoids a breaking signature change in 2A.3.b/c when the eval path
    41	//! could land inside replay.

   178	
   179	    /// **W5-118 (Phase 4.8.H):** `CreateTable` op references invariants
   180	    /// the producer should have validated. Catches snapshot-vs-replay
   181	    /// divergence (e.g. snapshot already has the table; another producer
   182	    /// raced).
   183	    #[error("replay create-table rejected at op index {index}: {reason}")]
   184	    TableCreateRejected {
   185	        index: usize,
   186	        name: String,
   187	        reason: &'static str,
   188	    },
   189	
   190	    /// **W5-118 (Phase 4.8.H):** `DropTable` op references a missing
   191	    /// table. Surfaces snapshot-vs-replay divergence loudly per
   192	    /// no-fallbacks doctrine.
   193	    #[error("replay drop-table at op index {index}: table {name:?} not found")]
   194	    TableNotFound { index: usize, name: String },
   195	
   196	    /// **W5-121 (Phase 4.8.I.2):** `RenameColumn` op references a column
   197	    /// that doesn't exist in the target table (case-insensitive). Either
   198	    /// the source column was already dropped/renamed before this op, or
   199	    /// the op log has diverged from the snapshot.
   200	    #[error(
   201	        "replay rename-column at op index {index}: table {table:?} \
   202	         has no column {column:?}"
   203	    )]
   204	    TableColumnNotFound {
   205	        index: usize,
   206	        table: String,
   207	        column: String,
   208	    },
   209	
   210	    /// **W5-121 (Phase 4.8.I.2):** `RenameColumn` op was rejected by a
   211	    /// validation rule (target name already in the table, empty, etc.).
   212	    /// `reason` is a static string describing which invariant fired.
   213	    #[error("replay rename-column rejected at op index {index}: table {table:?} column {column:?} ({reason})")]
   214	    TableColumnRejected {
   215	        index: usize,
   216	        table: String,
   217	        column: String,
   218	        reason: &'static str,
   219	    },
   220	
   221	    /// **W5-122 (Phase 4.8.J):** `ResizeTable` op was rejected by a
   222	    /// validation rule (arithmetic mismatch, trailing-columns
   223	    /// mismatch, column-name collision, footprint overlap, etc.).
   224	    /// `reason` is a static string describing which invariant fired.
   225	    #[error("replay resize-table rejected at op index {index}: table {name:?} ({reason})")]
   226	    TableResizeRejected {
   227	        index: usize,
   228	        name: String,
   229	        reason: &'static str,
   230	    },
   231	
   232	    /// **W5-146 (Phase 4.9.J):** `Op::SetLocale` wire value didn't
   233	    /// match any known locale code. Mirrors qbook v7's
   234	    /// `QbookError::UnknownLocale` (W5-145) — a forward-compat
   235	    /// op-log file with an unrecognized locale string surfaces this
   236	    /// instead of silently substituting EnUs (closes Sonnet L-10).
   237	    /// Captures the offending string for the IDE diagnostic.
   238	    #[error("replay unknown locale at op index {index}: {found:?}")]
   239	    UnknownLocale { index: usize, found: String },
   240	
   241	    /// **W5-151 (Phase 4.9.O MEDIUM-2 closure):** `Op::SetReferenceMode`
   242	    /// wire value didn't match `A1` or `R1C1`. Per design § 4.9.J,
   243	    /// the forward-compat path captures unknown strings into
   244	    /// `ReferenceModeWire::Unknown(_)` and replay surfaces this
   245	    /// distinct error rather than letting the op silently no-op.
   246	    /// Parallels `UnknownLocale` above.
   247	    #[error("replay unknown reference mode at op index {index}: {found:?}")]
   248	    UnknownReferenceMode { index: usize, found: String },
   249	}
   250	
   251	/// Wrapper around `ql_storage::FormatTableError` that owns its strings,
   252	/// so `ReplayError` can stay `Clone + std::error::Error` without
   253	/// borrowing into the table.
   254	///
   255	/// Phase 5.2 D-1 step 3: `id` / `existing_id` / `attempted_id` are now
   256	/// `ql_storage::FormatId` (tagged tuple) rather than the pre-step-3
   257	/// `u32`. Display formatting uses the FormatId's `Debug` impl so error
   258	/// messages identify both built-in and peer-allocated custom variants.
   259	#[derive(Clone, Debug, thiserror::Error)]
   260	#[non_exhaustive]
   261	pub enum FormatRejectedSource {
   262	    #[error("format id {id:?} already bound to {existing:?}, can't re-bind to {attempted:?}")]
   263	    IdCollision {
   264	        id: ql_storage::FormatId,
   265	        existing: String,
   266	        attempted: String,
   267	    },
   268	    #[error(
   269	        "format string {string:?} already at id {existing_id:?}, can't bind to id {attempted_id:?}"
   270	    )]
   271	    StringCollision {
   272	        string: String,
   273	        existing_id: ql_storage::FormatId,
   274	        attempted_id: ql_storage::FormatId,
   275	    },
   276	    /// **Phase 5.2 D-1 step 5 audit Codex HIGH-1 closure (2026-05-20):**
   277	    /// replayed `Op::RegisterFormat` with a `Custom(local_peer, u32::MAX)`
   278	    /// id would have panicked at `FormatTable::register_at`'s counter
   279	    /// advancement before this guard landed; now surfaces as a recoverable
   280	    /// replay error.
   281	    #[error("format counter overflow for peer {peer:?} (counter == u32::MAX)")]
   282	    CounterOverflow { peer: ql_types::PeerId },
   283	    /// **Phase 5.2 D-1 step 5 audit Codex HIGH-2 closure (2026-05-20):**
   284	    /// replayed `Op::RegisterFormat` with `Builtin(n > 163)`. Built-in
   285	    /// format ids are contractually `0..=FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX`;
   286	    /// `FormatIdWire::Builtin { id: u32 }` carries no range bound at the
   287	    /// type level so a malformed op can smuggle the bad shape past serde
   288	    /// validation. Surfaces here as a replay error rather than letting
   289	    /// the storage table silently accept and later drop the entry.
   290	    #[error(
   291	        "builtin format id {id} out of range (max {FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX})",
   292	        FIRST_XLSX_BUILTIN_MAX = 163
   293	    )]
   294	    BuiltinOutOfRange { id: u32 },
   295	}
   296	
   297	impl From<ql_storage::FormatTableError> for FormatRejectedSource {
   298	    fn from(e: ql_storage::FormatTableError) -> Self {
   299	        match e {
   300	            ql_storage::FormatTableError::IdCollision {
   301	                id,
   302	                existing,
   303	                attempted,
   304	            } => FormatRejectedSource::IdCollision {
   305	                id,
   306	                existing,
   307	                attempted,
   308	            },
   309	            ql_storage::FormatTableError::StringCollision {
   310	                string,
   311	                existing_id,
   312	                attempted_id,
   313	            } => FormatRejectedSource::StringCollision {
   314	                string,
   315	                existing_id,
   316	                attempted_id,
   317	            },
   318	            ql_storage::FormatTableError::CounterOverflow { peer } => {
   319	                FormatRejectedSource::CounterOverflow { peer }
   320	            }
   321	            ql_storage::FormatTableError::BuiltinOutOfRange { id } => {
   322	                FormatRejectedSource::BuiltinOutOfRange { id }
   323	            }
   324	            _ => unreachable!(
   325	                "FormatTableError gained a variant — extend FormatRejectedSource::From"
   326	            ),
   327	        }
   328	    }
   329	}
   330	
   331	/// Replay every op in `log` against `workbook` in append order.
   332	///
   333	/// Returns the total count of ops applied on success. On failure, the
   334	/// workbook is in a partial state — `ReplayError::At { index, .. }` tells
   335	/// the caller how far replay got.
   336	///
   337	/// The `registry` parameter is held for API symmetry with `WorkbookRuntime`
   338	/// and is unused in 2A.3.a (replay persists formula text without
   339	/// re-evaluating; callers drive evaluation through `recompute_all`).
   340	pub fn replay_into(
   341	    log: &OpLog,
   342	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
   343	    _registry: &FunctionRegistry,
   344	) -> Result<usize, ReplayError> {
   345	    let mut count = 0;
   346	    for (index, op_result) in log.iter().enumerate() {
   347	        let op = op_result.map_err(|e| ReplayError::Deserialize(index, e))?;
   348	        apply_op(&op, workbook, index)?;
   349	        count += 1;
   350	    }
   351	    Ok(count)
   352	}
   353	
   354	/// Recursive helper. `index` is the op's position in the outer log (or
   355	/// the synthetic position of the enclosing BatchCommit for nested ops —
   356	/// 2A.3.a flattens by reporting the parent's index for nested failures).
   357	fn apply_op(op: &Op, workbook: &mut Workbook, index: usize) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   358	    match op {
   359	        Op::PutValue {
   360	            sheet,
   361	            row,
   362	            col,
   363	            value,
   364	        } => {
   365	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   366	            let v: Value = value
   367	                .to_value()
   368	                .map_err(|source| ReplayError::ValueDecode { index, source })?;
   369	            workbook.put_at(*sheet, *row, *col, v);
   370	            Ok(())
   371	        }
   372	        Op::PutFormula {
   373	            sheet,
   374	            row,
   375	            col,
   376	            text,
   377	        } => {
   378	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   379	            workbook.put_formula(*sheet, *row, *col, text.as_str());
   380	            Ok(())
   381	        }
   382	        Op::ClearFormula { sheet, row, col } => {
   383	            // clear_formula is idempotent on missing entries; we still
   384	            // validate bounds so a corrupted op-log can't sneak past.
   385	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   386	            workbook.clear_formula(*sheet, *row, *col);
   387	            Ok(())
   388	        }
   389	        Op::SetName {
   390	            scope,
   391	            name,
   392	            target,
   393	        } => {
   394	            let target = target
   395	                .to_target(name)
   396	                .map_err(|source| ReplayError::NamedTargetDecode { index, source })?;
   397	            match scope {
   398	                None => {
   399	                    // Workbook-scoped (historical path).
   400	                    workbook.set_name(name, target).map_err(|source| {
   401	                        ReplayError::NameRejected {
   402	                            index,
   403	                            name: name.clone(),
   404	                            source,
   405	                        }
   406	                    })?;
   407	                }
   408	                Some(sheet) => {
   409	                    // **W5-92 (Phase 4.6.D):** sheet-scoped. Validate sheet
   410	                    // first so an unknown id surfaces as InvalidSheet, not
   411	                    // a panicking out-of-bounds index.
   412	                    let sheet_count = workbook.sheet_count();
   413	                    let sheet_ref =
   414	                        workbook
   415	                            .sheet_mut(*sheet)
   416	                            .ok_or(ReplayError::InvalidSheet {
   417	                                index,
   418	                                sheet: *sheet,
   419	                                sheet_count,
   420	                            })?;
   421	                    sheet_ref.set_scoped_name(name, target).map_err(|source| {
   422	                        ReplayError::NameRejected {
   423	                            index,
   424	                            name: name.clone(),
   425	                            source,
   426	                        }
   427	                    })?;
   428	                }
   429	            }
   430	            Ok(())
   431	        }
   432	        Op::AddSheet { name, chunk_rows } => {
   433	            // **W5-93 (Phase 4.6.E closure):** route through the fallible
   434	            // `try_add_sheet_with_chunk_rows` and surface a clean
   435	            // `ReplayError::SheetNameRejected` on validation failure.
   436	            // Codex HIGH-1 flagged that the prior infallible path
   437	            // silently accepted duplicate-canonical names + reserved
   438	            // characters at the replay boundary too.
   439	            //
   440	            // **Phase 5.2 D-2 closure (2026-05-19):** auto-rename on
   441	            // duplicate-canonical-name. Phase 5 multi-peer scenario:
   442	            // peer A and peer B both call `add_sheet("S")` locally;
   443	            // each producer-side validates against its own snapshot
   444	            // (no collision visible); both emit
   445	            // `Op::AddSheet { name: "S", ... }`; merged log has both.
   446	            // First replay succeeds; second hits the duplicate guard.
   447	            // Pre-D-2 we rejected the second op (worse UX than Google
   448	            // Sheets, which auto-renames to S(2)). Now we walk
   449	            // `<name>(2)`, `<name>(3)`, … until we find a free name.
   450	            // `Empty` + `ReservedCharacter` still reject — auto-rename
   451	            // only resolves the collaboration-collision case.
   452	            let mut chosen = name.clone();
   453	            let mut suffix = 2u32;
   454	            const AUTO_RENAME_CEILING: u32 = 10_000;
   455	            loop {
   456	                match workbook.try_add_sheet_with_chunk_rows(chosen.clone(), *chunk_rows) {
   457	                    Ok(_) => return Ok(()),
   458	                    Err(ql_storage::SheetNameError::Duplicate { .. }) => {
   459	                        chosen = format!("{name}({suffix})");
   460	                        suffix += 1;
   461	                        if suffix > AUTO_RENAME_CEILING {
   462	                            // Pathological: more than 10k sheets all
   463	                            // share the same base name (impossible in
   464	                            // realistic workbooks; max sheets per
   465	                            // workbook is 65,535). Surface a clean
   466	                            // error rather than loop forever.
   467	                            return Err(ReplayError::SheetNameRejected {
   468	                                index,
   469	                                name: name.clone(),
   470	                                source: ql_storage::SheetNameError::Duplicate {
   471	                                    name: name.clone(),
   472	                                },
   473	                            });
   474	                        }
   475	                    }
   476	                    Err(other) => {
   477	                        return Err(ReplayError::SheetNameRejected {
   478	                            index,
   479	                            name: name.clone(),
   480	                            source: other,
   481	                        });
   482	                    }
   483	                }
   484	            }
   485	        }
   486	        Op::RenameSheet {
   487	            id,
   488	            old_name,
   489	            new_name,
   490	        } => {
   491	            // **W5-91 (Phase 4.6.C):** snapshot-vs-replay reconciliation
   492	            // per design § 3.3. Three cases:
   493	            //   1. Current sheet name == old_name → fresh rename; apply.
   494	            //   2. Current sheet name == new_name → already-renamed (likely
   495	            //      replay-on-top-of-snapshot where the snapshot captured
   496	            //      the post-rename state). No-op; success.
   497	            //   3. Current sheet name == neither → divergent state; treat as
   498	            //      InvalidSheet for the op-log's safety contract.
   499	            let current = workbook.sheet(*id).map(|s| s.name().to_owned()).ok_or(
   500	                ReplayError::InvalidSheet {
   501	                    index,
   502	                    sheet: *id,
   503	                    sheet_count: workbook.sheet_count(),
   504	                },
   505	            )?;
   506	            let canonical = |s: &str| ql_storage::Workbook::canonical_sheet_name(s);
   507	            let cur_c = canonical(&current);
   508	            let old_c = canonical(old_name);
   509	            let new_c = canonical(new_name);
   510	            if cur_c == new_c {
   511	                // Already renamed (snapshot-authoritative path). No-op.
   512	                Ok(())
   513	            } else if cur_c == old_c {
   514	                workbook
   515	                    .rename_sheet(*id, new_name.clone())
   516	                    .map_err(|source| ReplayError::SheetRenameRejected {
   517	                        index,
   518	                        id: *id,
   519	                        old_name: old_name.clone(),
   520	                        new_name: new_name.clone(),
   521	                        source,
   522	                    })?;
   523	                Ok(())
   524	            } else {
   525	                Err(ReplayError::SheetRenameNameMismatch {
   526	                    index,
   527	                    id: *id,
   528	                    expected: old_name.clone(),
   529	                    found: current,
   530	                })
   531	            }
   532	        }
   533	        Op::RegisterFormat { id, string } => {
   534	            // **W5-80:** route through `FormatTable::register_at` so
   535	            // collisions surface as `FormatRejected` (rather than the
   536	            // panic-on-duplicate behavior `intern` would have via the
   537	            // by_string fast path; `register_at` is the explicit-id form).
   538	            //
   539	            // Phase 5.2 D-1 step 4: `Op::RegisterFormat.id` is now
   540	            // `FormatIdWire`. Convert to `ql_storage::FormatId` via
   541	            // `to_storage()`. The pre-step-4 `legacy_from_u32` migration
   542	            // helper is no longer needed for the wire-replay path; it's
   543	            // reserved for envelope-load migration in step 5.
   544	            let fid = id.to_storage();
   545	            workbook
   546	                .formats_mut()
   547	                .register_at(fid, string.as_str())
   548	                .map_err(|e| ReplayError::FormatRejected {
   549	                    index,
   550	                    source: e.into(),
   551	                })?;
   552	            Ok(())
   553	        }
   554	        Op::SetCellFormat {
   555	            sheet,
   556	            row,
   557	            col,
   558	            id,
   559	        } => {
   560	            validate_cell(workbook, *sheet, *row, *col, index)?;
   561	            // **W5-80:** require the id to be registered. Catches
   562	            // producer bugs where `SetCellFormat` was emitted without
   563	            // a preceding `RegisterFormat`. `None` means clear.
   564	            if let Some(wire_id) = id {
   565	                // Phase 5.2 D-1 step 4: same wire→storage conversion.
   566	                let fid = wire_id.to_storage();
   567	                if workbook.formats().lookup(fid).is_none() {
   568	                    return Err(ReplayError::FormatNotRegistered { index, id: fid });
   569	                }
   570	                workbook
   571	                    .sheet_mut(*sheet)
   572	                    .expect("sheet validated above")
   573	                    .format_overlay_mut()
   574	                    .set(*row, *col, fid);
   575	            } else {
   576	                workbook
   577	                    .sheet_mut(*sheet)
   578	                    .expect("sheet validated above")
   579	                    .format_overlay_mut()
   580	                    .clear(*row, *col);
   581	            }
   582	            Ok(())
   583	        }
   584	        Op::BatchCommit { ops } => {
   585	            for inner_op in ops {
   586	                // Phase 2A.3.a: nested ops flatten to the parent's index
   587	                // for error reporting. Phase 5+ may extend with
   588	                // (outer, inner) tuple indexing once the producer side
   589	                // emits nested commits in practice.
   590	                apply_op(inner_op, workbook, index)?;
   591	            }
   592	            Ok(())
   593	        }
   594	        Op::CreateTable {
   595	            name,
   596	            sheet,
   597	            top_row,
   598	            top_col,
   599	            rows,
   600	            cols,
   601	            has_header,
   602	            has_totals,
   603	            column_names,
   604	        } => apply_create_table(
   605	            workbook,
   606	            index,
   607	            name,
   608	            *sheet,
   609	            *top_row,
   610	            *top_col,
   611	            *rows,
   612	            *cols,
   613	            *has_header,
   614	            *has_totals,
   615	            column_names,
   616	        ),
   617	        Op::DropTable { name } => {
   618	            let canonical = name.to_ascii_uppercase();
   619	            if workbook.tables_mut().remove(canonical.as_str()).is_none() {
   620	                return Err(ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   621	                    index,
   622	                    name: name.clone(),
   623	                });
   624	            }
   625	            Ok(())
   626	        }
   627	        Op::RenameTable { old_name, new_name } => {
   628	            apply_rename_table(workbook, index, old_name, new_name)
   629	        }
   630	        Op::RenameColumn {
   631	            table,
   632	            old_name,
   633	            new_name,
   634	        } => apply_rename_column(workbook, index, table, old_name, new_name),
   635	        Op::ResizeTable {
   636	            name,
   637	            new_rows,
   638	            new_cols,
   639	            added_columns,
   640	            removed_columns,
   641	        } => apply_resize_table(
   642	            workbook,
   643	            index,
   644	            name,
   645	            *new_rows,
   646	            *new_cols,
   647	            added_columns,
   648	            removed_columns,
   649	        ),
   650	        // **W5-146 (Phase 4.9.J) + W5-151 (4.9.O MEDIUM-2 closure):**
   651	        // workbook-scope reference-mode change. Forward-compat
   652	        // unknown wire values surface `ReplayError::UnknownReferenceMode`
   653	        // with the captured string (mirrors the `LocaleWire::Unknown`
   654	        // path below).
   655	        Op::SetReferenceMode { mode } => match mode.clone().to_runtime() {
   656	            Ok(m) => {
   657	                workbook.set_reference_mode(m);
   658	                Ok(())
   659	            }
   660	            Err(found) => Err(ReplayError::UnknownReferenceMode { index, found }),
   661	        },
   662	        // **W5-146 (Phase 4.9.J):** workbook-scope locale change.
   663	        // Unknown wire values (forward-compat op-log file) surface
   664	        // `ReplayError::UnknownLocale` with the captured string.
   665	        Op::SetLocale { locale } => match locale.clone().to_runtime() {
   666	            Ok(loc) => {
   667	                workbook.set_locale(loc);
   668	                Ok(())
   669	            }
   670	            Err(found) => Err(ReplayError::UnknownLocale { index, found }),
   671	        },
   672	    }
   673	}
   674	
   675	/// **W5-119 (Phase 4.8.I):** replay a `RenameTable`. Validates source
   676	/// exists, target name is available (TableTable + NameTable shared
   677	/// namespace), then re-keys the entry. Note: formula text rewrites
   678	/// arrive as accompanying `Op::PutFormula` ops; this arm doesn't
   679	/// touch formula cells.
   680	fn apply_rename_table(
   681	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
   682	    index: usize,
   683	    old_name: &str,
   684	    new_name: &str,
   685	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   686	    let old_canonical = old_name.to_ascii_uppercase();
   687	    let new_canonical: std::sync::Arc<str> =
   688	        std::sync::Arc::from(new_name.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str());
   689	
   690	    // Verify source.
   691	    if workbook.tables().lookup(&old_canonical).is_none() {
   692	        return Err(ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   693	            index,
   694	            name: old_name.to_owned(),
   695	        });
   696	    }
   697	    // Verify target availability (skip the no-op same-name case).
   698	    if !old_canonical.eq_ignore_ascii_case(new_name) {
   699	        if workbook.tables().lookup(&new_canonical).is_some() {
   700	            return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   701	                index,
   702	                name: new_name.to_owned(),
   703	                reason: "table with this canonical name already exists (rename target)",
   704	            });
   705	        }
   706	        if workbook.names().lookup_ci(&new_canonical).is_some() {
   707	            return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   708	                index,
   709	                name: new_name.to_owned(),
   710	                reason: "defined-name with this canonical name already exists (rename target)",
   711	            });
   712	        }
   713	    }
   714	    // Take the entry out, mutate name + display, reinsert under new key.
   715	    let mut meta = workbook
   716	        .tables_mut()
   717	        .remove(&old_canonical)
   718	        .expect("verified above");
   719	    meta.name = std::sync::Arc::clone(&new_canonical);
   720	    meta.display_name = std::sync::Arc::from(new_name);
   721	    workbook.tables_mut().insert(new_canonical, meta);
   722	    Ok(())
   723	}
   724	
   725	/// **W5-121 (Phase 4.8.I.2):** replay a `RenameColumn`. Validates the
   726	/// target table exists, the source column exists (case-insensitive), and
   727	/// the target column name is available within the table. Mutates the
   728	/// matching `TableColumn`'s `name` (lowercase canonical) and `display`
   729	/// (case-preserving). Bumps the `TableTable` generation so plan caches
   730	/// invalidate. Same-canonical column renames are rejected — the producer
   731	/// side treats those as a no-op and doesn't emit the op, so receiving
   732	/// one indicates log divergence.
   733	fn apply_rename_column(
   734	    workbook: &mut ql_storage::Workbook,
   735	    index: usize,
   736	    table: &str,
   737	    old_name: &str,
   738	    new_name: &str,
   739	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   740	    let table_canonical = table.to_ascii_uppercase();
   741	    let meta = workbook
   742	        .tables_mut()
   743	        .get_mut(&table_canonical)
   744	        .ok_or_else(|| ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   745	            index,
   746	            name: table.to_owned(),
   747	        })?;
   748	    let (col_idx, _) =
   749	        meta.lookup_column(old_name)
   750	            .ok_or_else(|| ReplayError::TableColumnNotFound {
   751	                index,
   752	                table: table.to_owned(),
   753	                column: old_name.to_owned(),
   754	            })?;
   755	    if new_name.is_empty() {
   756	        return Err(ReplayError::TableColumnRejected {
   757	            index,
   758	            table: table.to_owned(),
   759	            column: new_name.to_owned(),
   760	            reason: "column name cannot be empty",
   761	        });
   762	    }
   763	    let old_lower = old_name.to_ascii_lowercase();
   764	    let new_lower = new_name.to_ascii_lowercase();
   765	    if old_lower == new_lower {
   766	        return Err(ReplayError::TableColumnRejected {
   767	            index,
   768	            table: table.to_owned(),
   769	            column: new_name.to_owned(),
   770	            reason: "rename to same canonical column name (producer should not emit)",
   771	        });
   772	    }
   773	    if meta.lookup_column(new_name).is_some() {
   774	        return Err(ReplayError::TableColumnRejected {
   775	            index,
   776	            table: table.to_owned(),
   777	            column: new_name.to_owned(),
   778	            reason: "column with this canonical name already exists (rename target)",
   779	        });
   780	    }
   781	    meta.columns[col_idx as usize].name = std::sync::Arc::from(new_lower.as_str());
   782	    meta.columns[col_idx as usize].display = std::sync::Arc::from(new_name);
   783	    workbook.tables_mut().bump_generation();
   784	    Ok(())
   785	}
   786	
   787	/// **W5-122 (Phase 4.8.J):** replay a `ResizeTable`. Validates the
   788	/// target table exists, the arithmetic invariant
   789	/// (`new_cols == old_cols + added.len() - removed.len()`),
   790	/// `removed_columns` exactly match the current trailing columns
   791	/// (case-insensitive on display), the final column roster has unique
   792	/// canonical names, and the new footprint cells outside the old
   793	/// footprint don't overlap other tables. Mutates the table metadata
   794	/// in place (rows/cols + columns vec). Bumps `TableTable` generation.
   795	fn apply_resize_table(
   796	    workbook: &mut ql_storage::Workbook,
   797	    index: usize,
   798	    name: &str,
   799	    new_rows: u32,
   800	    new_cols: u32,
   801	    added_columns: &[String],
   802	    removed_columns: &[String],
   803	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   804	    use ql_storage::TableColumn;
   805	    let canonical = name.to_ascii_uppercase();
   806	    // Snapshot the immutable bits we need to validate before mutating.
   807	    let (sheet, top_row, top_col, old_rows, old_cols, old_displays) = {
   808	        let meta =
   809	            workbook
   810	                .tables()
   811	                .lookup(&canonical)
   812	                .ok_or_else(|| ReplayError::TableNotFound {
   813	                    index,
   814	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   815	                })?;
   816	        (
   817	            meta.sheet,
   818	            meta.top_row,
   819	            meta.top_col,
   820	            meta.rows,
   821	            meta.cols,
   822	            meta.columns
   823	                .iter()
   824	                .map(|c| c.display.as_ref().to_owned())
   825	                .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
   826	        )
   827	    };
   828	    if new_rows == 0 || new_cols == 0 {
   829	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   830	            index,
   831	            name: name.to_owned(),
   832	            reason: "table rows and cols must both be > 0",
   833	        });
   834	    }
   835	    // **W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 — Codex HIGH-1):** validate footprint
   836	    // upper bound mirrors producer side.
   837	    if let Err(reason) =
   838	        ql_storage::TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds(top_row, top_col, new_rows, new_cols)
   839	    {
   840	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   841	            index,
   842	            name: name.to_owned(),
   843	            reason,
   844	        });
   845	    }
   846	    let added_len = added_columns.len() as u32;
   847	    let removed_len = removed_columns.len() as u32;
   848	    if removed_len > old_cols {
   849	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   850	            index,
   851	            name: name.to_owned(),
   852	            reason: "removed_columns count exceeds existing column count",
   853	        });
   854	    }
   855	    // Arithmetic invariant.
   856	    if new_cols != old_cols + added_len - removed_len {
   857	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   858	            index,
   859	            name: name.to_owned(),
   860	            reason: "new_cols does not match old_cols + added - removed",
   861	        });
   862	    }
   863	    // removed_columns must exactly match trailing displays
   864	    // (case-insensitive).
   865	    let trailing_start = (old_cols - removed_len) as usize;
   866	    for (i, expected) in removed_columns.iter().enumerate() {
   867	        let idx = trailing_start + i;
   868	        if !old_displays[idx].eq_ignore_ascii_case(expected) {
   869	            return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   870	                index,
   871	                name: name.to_owned(),
   872	                reason: "removed_columns do not match trailing columns",
   873	            });
   874	        }
   875	    }
   876	    // added_columns: non-empty + unique vs final roster.
   877	    if added_columns.iter().any(|s| s.is_empty()) {
   878	        return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   879	            index,
   880	            name: name.to_owned(),
   881	            reason: "added column names cannot be empty",
   882	        });
   883	    }
   884	    // Build the final canonical (lowercase) roster.
   885	    let mut final_canon: Vec<String> = old_displays
   886	        .iter()
   887	        .take(trailing_start)
   888	        .map(|d| d.to_ascii_lowercase())
   889	        .collect();
   890	    for a in added_columns {
   891	        final_canon.push(a.to_ascii_lowercase());
   892	    }
   893	    {
   894	        use std::collections::HashSet;
   895	        let mut seen: HashSet<&str> = HashSet::new();
   896	        for cn in &final_canon {
   897	            if !seen.insert(cn.as_str()) {
   898	                return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   899	                    index,
   900	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   901	                    reason: "final column roster has duplicate canonical names",
   902	                });
   903	            }
   904	        }
   905	    }
   906	    // Footprint-overlap check: only cells NEWLY claimed by this resize
   907	    // need checking. Old-footprint cells already belong to this table.
   908	    // We test all cells in [top_row..top_row+new_rows] x [top_col..
   909	    // top_col+new_cols] and skip those inside the OLD footprint.
   910	    let old_end_row = top_row + old_rows;
   911	    let old_end_col = top_col + old_cols;
   912	    let new_end_row = top_row + new_rows;
   913	    let new_end_col = top_col + new_cols;
   914	    for r in top_row..new_end_row {
   915	        for c in top_col..new_end_col {
   916	            let inside_old = r < old_end_row && c < old_end_col;
   917	            if inside_old {
   918	                continue;
   919	            }
   920	            if let Some(other) = workbook.table_at(sheet, r, c) {
   921	                if !other.name.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&canonical) {
   922	                    return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   923	                        index,
   924	                        name: name.to_owned(),
   925	                        reason: "new footprint overlaps an existing table",
   926	                    });
   927	                }
   928	            }
   929	            // **W5-124 (Phase 4.8.J.2):** spill-anchor check mirrors
   930	            // producer side. Per design § 4.3 invariant #5, tables
   931	            // block ALL spill anchors inside their footprint.
   932	            if workbook.spill_anchor_at(sheet, r, c).is_some() {
   933	                return Err(ReplayError::TableResizeRejected {
   934	                    index,
   935	                    name: name.to_owned(),
   936	                    reason: "new footprint contains a spill anchor",
   937	                });
   938	            }
   939	        }
   940	    }
   941	    // ----- Mutation -----
   942	    // Allocate new column ids BEFORE taking &mut on the table entry
   943	    // (allocate_column_id lives on TableTable not TableMetadata).
   944	    let new_ids: Vec<u32> = (0..added_columns.len())
   945	        .map(|_| workbook.tables_mut().allocate_column_id())
   946	        .collect();
   947	    let meta = workbook
   948	        .tables_mut()
   949	        .get_mut(&canonical)
   950	        .expect("verified at top");
   951	    meta.rows = new_rows;
   952	    meta.cols = new_cols;
   953	    meta.columns
   954	        .truncate(meta.columns.len() - removed_len as usize);
   955	    for (cn, id) in added_columns.iter().zip(new_ids) {
   956	        meta.columns.push(TableColumn {
   957	            id,
   958	            name: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str()),
   959	            display: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.as_str()),
   960	            totals_function: None,
   961	        });
   962	    }
   963	    workbook.tables_mut().bump_generation();
   964	    Ok(())
   965	}
   966	
   967	/// **W5-118 (Phase 4.8.H):** apply a `CreateTable` op against the
   968	/// workbook. Validates the same invariants the producer side checks
   969	/// (mirror via `WorkbookRuntime::create_table`).
   970	#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
   971	fn apply_create_table(
   972	    workbook: &mut Workbook,
   973	    index: usize,
   974	    name: &str,
   975	    sheet: SheetId,
   976	    top_row: RowId,
   977	    top_col: ColId,
   978	    rows: u32,
   979	    cols: u32,
   980	    has_header: bool,
   981	    has_totals: bool,
   982	    column_names: &[String],
   983	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
   984	    use ql_storage::{TableColumn, TableMetadata};
   985	    let canonical: std::sync::Arc<str> = std::sync::Arc::from(name.to_ascii_uppercase().as_str());
   986	    if workbook.tables().lookup(&canonical).is_some() {
   987	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   988	            index,
   989	            name: name.to_owned(),
   990	            reason: "table with this canonical name already exists",
   991	        });
   992	    }
   993	    if workbook.names().lookup_ci(&canonical).is_some() {
   994	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
   995	            index,
   996	            name: name.to_owned(),
   997	            reason: "defined-name with this canonical name already exists (shared namespace)",
   998	        });
   999	    }
  1000	    if column_names.len() != cols as usize {
  1001	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1002	            index,
  1003	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1004	            reason: "column_names length does not match cols",
  1005	        });
  1006	    }
  1007	    if column_names.iter().any(|s| s.is_empty()) {
  1008	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1009	            index,
  1010	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1011	            reason: "table column names cannot be empty",
  1012	        });
  1013	    }
  1014	    // Column-name uniqueness (case-insensitive).
  1015	    {
  1016	        use std::collections::HashSet;
  1017	        let mut seen: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
  1018	        for cn in column_names {
  1019	            if !seen.insert(cn.to_ascii_lowercase()) {
  1020	                return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1021	                    index,
  1022	                    name: name.to_owned(),
  1023	                    reason: "table column names must be unique (case-insensitive)",
  1024	                });
  1025	            }
  1026	        }
  1027	    }
  1028	    if workbook.sheet(sheet).is_none() {
  1029	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1030	            index,
  1031	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1032	            reason: "table references unknown sheet",
  1033	        });
  1034	    }
  1035	    if rows == 0 || cols == 0 {
  1036	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1037	            index,
  1038	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1039	            reason: "table rows and cols must both be > 0",
  1040	        });
  1041	    }
  1042	    // **W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 — Codex HIGH-1):** validate footprint
  1043	    // upper bound mirrors producer side.
  1044	    if let Err(reason) =
  1045	        ql_storage::TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds(top_row, top_col, rows, cols)
  1046	    {
  1047	        return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1048	            index,
  1049	            name: name.to_owned(),
  1050	            reason,
  1051	        });
  1052	    }
  1053	    // Non-overlap + no-spill-anchor inside the footprint.
  1054	    // **W5-124 (Phase 4.8.J.2):** spill-anchor check mirrors producer
  1055	    // side per design § 4.3 invariant #5.
  1056	    for r in top_row..top_row + rows {
  1057	        for c in top_col..top_col + cols {
  1058	            if workbook.table_at(sheet, r, c).is_some() {
  1059	                return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1060	                    index,
  1061	                    name: name.to_owned(),
  1062	                    reason: "table footprint overlaps an existing table",
  1063	                });
  1064	            }
  1065	            if workbook.spill_anchor_at(sheet, r, c).is_some() {
  1066	                return Err(ReplayError::TableCreateRejected {
  1067	                    index,
  1068	                    name: name.to_owned(),
  1069	                    reason: "table footprint contains a spill anchor",
  1070	                });
  1071	            }
  1072	        }
  1073	    }
  1074	    // Build columns with freshly-allocated ids.
  1075	    let columns: Vec<TableColumn> = column_names
  1076	        .iter()
  1077	        .map(|cn| TableColumn {
  1078	            id: workbook.tables_mut().allocate_column_id(),
  1079	            name: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str()),
  1080	            display: std::sync::Arc::from(cn.as_str()),
  1081	            totals_function: None,
  1082	        })
  1083	        .collect();
  1084	    let meta = TableMetadata {
  1085	        name: canonical.clone(),
  1086	        display_name: std::sync::Arc::from(name),
  1087	        sheet,
  1088	        top_row,
  1089	        top_col,
  1090	        rows,
  1091	        cols,
  1092	        has_header,
  1093	        has_totals,
  1094	        columns,
  1095	    };
  1096	    workbook.tables_mut().insert(canonical, meta);
  1097	    Ok(())
  1098	}
  1099	
  1100	fn validate_cell(
  1101	    workbook: &Workbook,
  1102	    sheet: SheetId,
  1103	    row: RowId,
  1104	    col: ColId,
  1105	    index: usize,
  1106	) -> Result<(), ReplayError> {
  1107	    let count = workbook.sheet_count();
  1108	    if (sheet as usize) >= count {
  1109	        return Err(ReplayError::InvalidSheet {
  1110	            index,
  1111	            sheet,
  1112	            sheet_count: count,
  1113	        });
  1114	    }
  1115	    if row > MAX_ROW {
  1116	        return Err(ReplayError::InvalidCell {
  1117	            index,
  1118	            row,
  1119	            col,
  1120	            why: "row exceeds MAX_ROW (1,048,575)",
  1121	        });
  1122	    }
  1123	    if col > MAX_COLUMN {
  1124	        return Err(ReplayError::InvalidCell {
  1125	            index,
  1126	            row,
  1127	            col,
  1128	            why: "col exceeds MAX_COLUMN (16,383)",
  1129	        });
  1130	    }
  1131	    Ok(())
  1132	}

  1134	#[cfg(test)]
  1135	mod tests {
  1136	    use super::*;
  1137	    use crate::wire::{CellWireValue, NamedTargetWire};
  1138	    use ql_functions::default_registry;
  1139	    use ql_storage::NamedTarget;
  1140	    use ql_types::Address;
  1141	
  1142	    fn fresh_workbook_with_one_sheet() -> Workbook {
  1143	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1144	        wb.add_sheet("S");
  1145	        wb
  1146	    }
  1147	
  1148	    #[test]
  1149	    fn replay_empty_log_succeeds() {
  1150	        let log = OpLog::new();
  1151	        let mut wb = fresh_workbook_with_one_sheet();
  1152	        let reg = default_registry();
  1153	        let n = replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap();
  1154	        assert_eq!(n, 0);
  1155	    }
  1156	
  1157	    #[test]
  1158	    fn replay_put_value_lands_in_workbook() {

  1160	        log.append(Op::PutValue {
  1161	            sheet: 0,
  1162	            row: 5,
  1163	            col: 3,
  1164	            value: CellWireValue::Number(42.0),
  1165	        })
  1166	        .unwrap();
  1167	
  1168	        let mut wb = fresh_workbook_with_one_sheet();

  1173	    }
  1174	
  1175	    #[test]

  1189	        // Formula text persisted ...

  1191	        // ... value NOT evaluated (replay leaves recompute to the caller).

  1263	    fn replay_batch_commit_applies_inner_ops_in_order() {

  1680	    #[test]
  1681	    fn replay_rename_inside_batchcommit() {
  1682	        // Producer pattern: rewrite-then-rename batched as a single
  1683	        // BatchCommit. Verify the batch replays atomically.
  1684	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1685	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1686	            name: "S1".to_owned(),
  1687	            chunk_rows: 1024,
  1688	        })
  1689	        .unwrap();
  1690	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1691	            name: "S2".to_owned(),
  1692	            chunk_rows: 1024,
  1693	        })
  1694	        .unwrap();
  1695	        log.append(Op::PutFormula {
  1696	            sheet: 1, // S2!A1
  1697	            row: 0,
  1698	            col: 0,
  1699	            text: "S1!A1 + 1".to_owned(),
  1700	        })
  1701	        .unwrap();
  1702	        log.append(Op::BatchCommit {
  1703	            ops: vec![
  1704	                Op::PutFormula {
  1705	                    sheet: 1,
  1706	                    row: 0,
  1707	                    col: 0,
  1708	                    text: "SX!A1 + 1".to_owned(),
  1709	                },
  1710	                Op::RenameSheet {
  1711	                    id: 0,
  1712	                    old_name: "S1".to_owned(),
  1713	                    new_name: "SX".to_owned(),
  1714	                },
  1715	            ],
  1716	        })
  1717	        .unwrap();
  1718	
  1719	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1720	        let reg = default_registry();
  1721	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap();
  1722	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "SX");
  1723	        assert_eq!(
  1724	            wb.formula_at(1, 0, 0).map(|s| s.as_ref().to_owned()),
  1725	            Some("SX!A1 + 1".to_owned())
  1726	        );
  1727	    }

  1831	    fn replay_add_sheet_canonical_duplicate_auto_renames() {
  1832	        // **Phase 5.2 D-2 closure (2026-05-19):** auto-rename replaces
  1833	        // the pre-D-2 behavior of rejecting duplicate-canonical names
  1834	        // at replay. Phase 5 collaboration scenario: peer A and peer B
  1835	        // both call `add_sheet("Sheet1")` locally with no collision
  1836	        // visible at producer time; both append the op; merged log
  1837	        // has both. Per the Google Sheets / Excel Online pattern, the
  1838	        // second auto-renames to `Sheet1(2)` rather than rejecting.
  1839	        //
  1840	        // Pre-D-2 this test was `replay_add_sheet_canonical_duplicate_rejected`
  1841	        // asserting `ReplayError::SheetNameRejected`. The D-2 spec
  1842	        // (5.1 audit Opus H-3) inverted that expectation.
  1843	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1844	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1845	            name: "Sheet1".to_owned(),
  1846	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1847	        })
  1848	        .unwrap();
  1849	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1850	            name: "SHEET1".to_owned(),
  1851	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1852	        })
  1853	        .unwrap();
  1854	
  1855	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1856	        let reg = default_registry();
  1857	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).expect("auto-rename succeeds");
  1858	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet_count(), 2);
  1859	        // First sheet keeps its name.
  1860	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1");
  1861	        // Second sheet auto-renamed (original was "SHEET1" which is
  1862	        // a canonical-duplicate of "Sheet1"; suffix starts at (2)).
  1863	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(1).unwrap().name(), "SHEET1(2)");
  1864	    }
  1865	
  1866	    #[test]
  1867	    fn replay_add_sheet_auto_rename_walks_suffix_until_free() {
  1868	        // Three peers concurrently add "Sheet1"; replay should
  1869	        // produce Sheet1, Sheet1(2), Sheet1(3).
  1870	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1871	        for _ in 0..3 {
  1872	            log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1873	                name: "Sheet1".to_owned(),
  1874	                chunk_rows: 16,
  1875	            })
  1876	            .unwrap();
  1877	        }
  1878	
  1879	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1880	        let reg = default_registry();
  1881	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap();
  1882	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet_count(), 3);
  1883	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1");
  1884	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(1).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1(2)");
  1885	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(2).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1(3)");
  1886	    }

  1889	    fn replay_add_sheet_auto_rename_skips_already_taken_suffix() {
  1890	        // Pre-existing "Sheet1(2)" forces the second AddSheet("Sheet1")
  1891	        // to skip to (3). Verifies the loop genuinely walks until
  1892	        // it finds a free slot.
  1893	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1894	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1895	            name: "Sheet1".to_owned(),
  1896	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1897	        })
  1898	        .unwrap();
  1899	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1900	            name: "Sheet1(2)".to_owned(),
  1901	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1902	        })
  1903	        .unwrap();
  1904	        log.append(Op::AddSheet {
  1905	            name: "Sheet1".to_owned(),
  1906	            chunk_rows: 16,
  1907	        })
  1908	        .unwrap();
  1909	
  1910	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1911	        let reg = default_registry();
  1912	        replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap();
  1913	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet_count(), 3);
  1914	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(0).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1");
  1915	        assert_eq!(wb.sheet(1).unwrap().name(), "Sheet1(2)");

  1920	        );

  1968	    /// **Unknown locale wire value (forward-compat) → loud error.**
  1969	    /// Closes Sonnet L-10. The `LocaleWire` deserializer captures
  1970	    /// unknown strings into `Unknown(s)`; replay surfaces them as
  1971	    /// `ReplayError::UnknownLocale { index, found }`.
  1972	    #[test]
  1973	    fn replay_set_locale_unknown_value_errors_loudly() {
  1974	        let mut log = OpLog::new();
  1975	        log.append(Op::SetLocale {
  1976	            locale: crate::op::LocaleWire::Unknown("xx".to_string()),
  1977	        })
  1978	        .unwrap();
  1979	        let mut wb = Workbook::new();
  1980	        let reg = default_registry();
  1981	        let err = replay_into(&log, &mut wb, &reg).unwrap_err();
  1982	        match err {
  1983	            ReplayError::UnknownLocale { index, found } => {
  1984	                assert_eq!(index, 0);
  1985	                assert_eq!(found, "xx");
  1986	            }
  1987	            other => panic!("expected UnknownLocale, got {other:?}"),
  1988	        }
  1989	    }
